name: Aly Packaging USA
old_description: Aly Packaging delivers durable, custom packaging for every business need across the USA with free quotes, samples, and unmatched industry expertise.
about:
Aly Packaging USA operates from New York, New York, as the U.S. arm of a packaging business that began in 2013 in Croydon, England. The company originated as an endeavor of Crushing Mart Ltd., a UK-based firm that spent over a decade serving British SMEs and corporations before expanding across the Atlantic. No individual founders are named in public materials.

The company manufactures custom packaging boxes across more than 80 categories, including cardboard, kraft, corrugated, and rigid constructions. It offers printing and finishing services such as foil stamping (gold, silver, holographic), spot UV, embossing, debossing, and soft-touch coating. Box styles range from tuck and sleeve to window and handle designs. The firm reports serving over a thousand brands and maintaining near-perfect delivery across thousands of orders, with countrywide distribution from its U.S. facility.

Aly Packaging serves startups, small-to-midsize enterprises, and corporate brands across what it describes as 250-plus industries. Testimonials reference clients in cosmetics, jewelry, small electronics, apparel, and pharmaceuticals, though no exhaustive industry list is published.

The company emphasizes free design support, free consultancy, and free shipping as core differentiators. It also offers prototype samples before full production and rush manufacturing options that can deliver in as few as six business days. The stated mission is to transform packaging into a growth-ready brand asset rather than mere product protection.

name: Amana Furniture Shop
old_description: Explore our Look Book for more Amana inspiration and information.
about:
Amana Furniture Shop operates in Amana, Iowa, a community within the historic Amana Colonies. The company traces its legacy of craftsmanship, sustainability, and community to 1855, when the colony’s artisans began producing furniture and household goods for communal use. While the current ownership structure is not publicly detailed, the business continues to emphasize its roots in the colony’s collective workshop tradition.

The shop manufactures a range of Iowa-made wood products, including end-grain cutting boards, gallery clocks, and charcuterie boards, all described as handcrafted. In addition to its own lines, the showroom carries American-made upholstered and leather furniture from partner brands Bradington-Young and Temple Furniture. The company runs a retail showroom at 724 48th Avenue and an online store, though facility size and employee count are not disclosed.

Amana Furniture Shop serves primarily residential customers seeking domestically produced furniture and kitchen accessories. Its product categories span furniture, home goods, and kitchenware, with concrete examples such as the Savanna Gallery Clock and end-grain cutting boards. The company also appeals to visitors of the Amana Colonies tourist area through its physical showroom.

The company states that its differentiation lies in a commitment to quality that has never wavered since 1855, linking each purchase to the craftsmen who build the products. It highlights sustainability and community as core values, positioning its goods as heirloom-quality items that support local artisans.

name: Amdek, Inc. - Pad Printing & Injection Molding
old_description: Precision Plastic Injection Molding & Pad Printing Since 1991
about:
Amdek, Inc. was founded in 1991 in Somerville, Alabama, when Robert Tetzlaff purchased RWT Plastics Systems from his father and renamed it Alabama Molding and Decorating. The company began with three Battenfeld injection molding machines and five customers. Now led by third-generation president Wolf Tetzlaff, the family-owned business operates a second facility in Sherwood, Oregon, acquired in 2016.

The company provides turnkey contract manufacturing, combining plastic injection molding, pad printing, tool design, and final assembly under one roof. Its Alabama and Oregon plants run Cincinnati Milacron presses ranging from 33 to 165 tons, including a Roboshot unit, and a large-format six-color pad printer added in 2024. Amdek handles short-run prototypes through high-volume production, with secondary operations and assembly integration.

Amdek serves medical, automotive, electronics, and industrial markets. A noted customer is Wilson Sporting Goods, for which the company has printed custom logos since 2009. The firm also produces its own Earth Friendly Cutlery line of compostable utensils.

Amdek emphasizes its BBB accreditation, dual-location logistics for faster delivery, and a design-first approach that optimizes parts before tooling. The company traces its roots to Robert Tetzlaff’s early career selling molding and pad-printing equipment, a background that shaped its focus on integrated decorating and molding solutions.

name: America's Food Equipment Co
old_description: We were founded in 1976 as a kitchen service company. Soon after, we began to manufacture kitchen hood systems under our  Ventex Air Systems logo.
about:
America's Food Equipment Co was founded in 1976 in Inman, South Carolina, initially as a kitchen service company. The business later expanded into manufacturing kitchen hood systems under its Ventex Air Systems brand.

Today the company designs commercial kitchens, supplies a range of restaurant equipment — including refrigerators, freezers, fryers, ranges, stoves, ice makers, and walk-in coolers — and provides installation services across the Southeast United States. It also ships kitchen equipment packages nationwide. Manufacturing remains focused on hood systems produced under the Ventex Air Systems label.

The company serves the foodservice and restaurant industries, working with operators who need complete kitchen design, equipment procurement, and installation. Its customer base includes independent restaurants and regional chains throughout the Southeast, with nationwide shipping available for equipment packages.

America's Food Equipment positions itself as a dealer for large kitchen equipment items, representing multiple established brands. The addition of in-house hood manufacturing was intended to complement its service and supply offerings, giving customers a single source for both custom ventilation and standard kitchen equipment.

about:
American Cable Inc operates as a local DISH retailer in the London, Kentucky area, with a physical address at 112 Pike Alley in Jamestown. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed. It appears to be an independent authorized dealer for DISH Network satellite television services.

The business sells DISH satellite TV packages—including America's Top 120, 200, and 250 channel tiers—and provides professional installation. It also offers Starlink residential internet service as an additional connectivity option. The retailer handles equipment such as the Hopper 3 DVR and promotes DISH's 2-year price guarantee, free standard installation, and HD for life.

The company targets residential customers in rural Kentucky communities, advertising special offers for seniors, military personnel, and front-line workers. Testimonials on its site reference customers in New London and Jamestown, indicating a local customer base.

The retailer emphasizes consistent, reliable local service and a commitment to staying in the community, echoing DISH's broader rural investment messaging. It highlights signal reliability with a money-back guarantee and the convenience of bundled TV and internet.

about:
American Eagle Food Machinery, Inc. is based in Chicago, Illinois, where it operates as a manufacturer of commercial food service equipment. The company’s founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company produces commercial food preparation equipment such as dough sheeters—highlighted by the AE-DS650B-SS model—and meat processing machines. Its equipment features heavy-duty, high-polished aluminum construction with a Teflon coating and a universal #12 hub that allows additional attachments. American Eagle also designs its own electronics and shielded wiring for reliable operation, and supplies accessories and replacement parts. Details on facility size, employee count, or production volumes are not available.

American Eagle’s equipment is aimed at the food service sector, including catering operations, commercial kitchens, and food preparation facilities. The company’s blog discusses the Chicago catering industry, indicating a focus on that market.

The company emphasizes quality, value, and reliability in its messaging, and offers toll-free service support. No further differentiation claims are provided.

name: American Electronics Components
old_description: A short sentence describing what someone will receive by subscribing
about:
Based in Boonton, New Jersey, American Electronics Components (AECI) operates as a global electronics company specializing in telecom and network infrastructure. The company sells a wide range of equipment from manufacturers such as Cisco, Lucent, AT&T, Foundry, Ceragon, and CommScope, and also provides asset recovery, facility closing, fulfillment, material management, and sourcing services.

AECI’s product catalog includes switches, routers, firewalls, microwave radio kits, cables, assemblies, and hardware such as ground bars and u-bolt assemblies. The company lists over 80 products across categories including network equipment, test equipment, antennas, power equipment, and infrastructure hardware. It also operates a fulfillment center and offers material management programs for customers downsizing or closing facilities.

The company serves telecommunications carriers, data centers, enterprise IT departments, and wireless network operators. Concrete examples from its inventory include AT&T PoE switches, Cisco Catalyst and ASR series modules, Lucent Ethernet processors, Ceragon 23 GHz remote mount kits, and CommScope grounding and mounting hardware.

AECI differentiates itself by combining product distribution with asset recovery and supply chain services, allowing customers to source both new and surplus equipment while managing end-of-life asset disposition.

name: American Embroidery
old_description: Welcome to American Embroidery, your go-to local source for all your custom embroidery,
about:
American Embroidery is a family-owned and operated business based in Berlin, Connecticut. Founded in 2003 by Lisa and Enzo Mariano, the company began in their basement before expanding to a storefront in downtown Berlin.

The shop provides custom embroidery, screen printing, and DTF heat transfer services for a wide range of apparel, bags, hats, safety gear, and promotional gifts, and also supplies the base garments such as twill shirts, denim shirts, jackets, and hats. Embroidery is produced in-house on Barudan machines capable of up to 15 colors per logo, while screen printing requires a minimum of 24 pieces per design. The facility handles orders ranging from single items to thousands of pieces, with no minimum on most embroidered and heat-transfer orders.

Customers include local businesses, schools, sports teams, first responders, construction firms, hunters, and charitable organizations. The company works closely with area businesses and organizations to supply branded apparel, safety vests, jackets, and custom giveaways for events and daily use.

The Marianos emphasize quick turnaround, competitive pricing, and a no-minimum policy on most items as key differentiators, aiming to accommodate both small and large orders with the same level of service.

about:
American Metal Fabrications, Inc. was established in 1992 in Richmond, Virginia. The company operates from a facility on Sisco Avenue and has served the region for over three decades.

The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication, offering CNC laser cutting, plasma cutting, and machine shop services. It also provides welding and small-scale installation work, supported by a team of 25 skilled employees. The facility handles projects ranging from single prototypes to large production runs.

The company works with customers across a variety of sectors that require precision sheet metal parts, though specific industries are not publicly listed. Its client base includes both large-scale and small-scale orders, reflecting a flexible production approach.

According to the company, its growth has been driven by a commitment to exceptional product quality and outstanding service, which it describes as its top priority and the main reason for its continued expansion.
